description: The Hydrological Service of the Israel Water Authority publishes its surface water monitoring data on the national open data portal. Contents: a list of active and inactive hydrometric observation stations; daily volumes in cubic metres and mean daily discharge in cubic metres per second per station, split into files from before 1960 to 2020 onward; instantaneous discharge hydrographs; historical annual maximum instantaneous discharges and annual volumes per stream station; water quality sampling at stations; and daily levels of Lake Kinneret (Sea of Galilee) and the Dead Sea. Producer: the Water Authority's Hydrological Service, which converts stage measurements to flow with rating curves. Coverage: Israeli streams and lakes, with records reaching back before 1960 and monthly or annual updates. Format and access: CSV downloads on data.gov.il and the CKAN datastore API. Licence: CC BY for the station lists, the portal's other open terms for most flow files. Free. Caveats: flows in ephemeral desert streams are highly flashy, so daily means understate flood peaks; station coordinates and names are in Hebrew and use the Israeli grid. Simulation uses: flash flood frequency analysis and design floods for roads, bridges and culverts, calibration of hydrological models, and water supply stress indicators from lake levels. Related records: none yet in the catalogue for Israeli hydrology.
